h1:
Mae Hong Son & Pai
on a Backpacker Budget
intro: Mae Hong Son and Pai really can be done cheap if you know the ropes — take the public minivan instead of chartering a car, rent a scooter for a hundred-odd baht a day, sleep in hostels for a few hundred, and eat at the morning market and local shops. This is a 3-day backpacker plan where we break down the real costs so you can see exactly how much the trip takes to be both worth it and fun.

blocks.html: Good news for anyone watching their wallet: Mae Hong Son and Pai aren't as pricey as you'd think. The real costs come down to just three things — transport there and back, accommodation, and scooter rental. Most of the sights in Pai and around Mae Hong Son town are free or charge a small entry fee of a few dozen baht. Food is cheap too if you eat like a local. For this trip we've planned it around taking the minivan from Chiang Mai, so you don't need your own car — ideal whether you're travelling solo or as a pair.

blocks.text: How much does this trip cost (a realistic estimate)

blocks.html: The figures below are based on 2025–2026 prices, assuming hostel stays, eating at local shops, and splitting the scooter if there are two of you. Use them as a rough frame to budget before you set off — actual prices shift with the season and the shop.

items: Chiang Mai–Pai minivan, return — about ฿300 (฿150 each way with Prempracha)
Pai–Mae Hong Son minivan, return — about ฿300 (if you continue on to Mae Hong Son town)
Hostel — ฿150–350 per night (dorm bed), or a budget double room ฿400–600
Scooter rental — ฿100–150 per day + ฿50–80 a day for fuel
Food — ฿200–300 per day if you stick to the morning market, rice-and-curry shops, and the walking street
Entry fees — no more than ฿200 for the whole trip (lots of places are free)

blocks.title: Total budget at a glance
blocks.html: A 3-day, 2-night trip focused on Pai alone can land around ฿2,000–2,800 per person. Add 1–2 days continuing to Mae Hong Son town and you're looking at another ฿1,000–1,500. What pushes it cheaper or pricier is whether you take a dorm bed and whether you can split the scooter.

blocks.text: How to get there for the least money

blocks.html: The key to doing this cheaply is not chartering a car — take the scheduled public minivan instead. The main operator people use is Prempracha Transport, which has run this route for years and runs frequent departures from Arcade bus station (Chang Phueak / Arcade 2) in Chiang Mai.

items: Chiang Mai → Pai — minivan around ฿150, roughly 132 km, about 3 hours. Several departures from morning to evening (roughly 07:30–17:30)
Pai → Mae Hong Son — fewer departures, just a few a day, so check times in advance, especially the morning ones
Chiang Mai → Mae Hong Son (direct) — minivans run via Pai as well, around 6–8 hours
Flying — there are Chiang Mai–Mae Hong Son flights, very short hops, but fares are unpredictable. Compare against the minivan first if you want to save time

blocks.title: For anyone who gets carsick
blocks.html: The Chiang Mai–Pai–Mae Hong Son route is a long stretch of mountain switchbacks (people like to call it the 1,864-curve road). If you're prone to motion sickness, take a tablet before you board, grab a seat near the front, and avoid eating a heavy meal right before you leave.

blocks.text: Where to sleep cheap with a good location

blocks.html: Pai is full of cheap hostels and guesthouses. The best-value spot to base yourself is around the Pai Walking Street, because you can walk to food and nightlife and skip the fuel costs. Dorm beds start in the low hundreds, and a budget private room runs about ฿400–600. Over in Mae Hong Son town, the guesthouses around Nong Jong Kham lake and Khunlumprapas Road come in at similar prices, with lake views right in the middle of town.

items: Pick a place near the Pai Walking Street — saves you the night-time travel, and you can walk out to dinner
Book ahead in the cool season — November to January gets busy, prices climb and rooms fill fast
Ask your accommodation about scooter rental — many will sort one out or point you to a shop with better rates than the walk-up price

blocks.text: Eat cheap but full — the shops and dishes worth your baht

blocks.html: Food is the easiest place to trim your budget. Stick to the morning market, local rice-and-curry shops, and the walking street, and ฿40–70 a meal will fill you up. Here are the budget-friendly dishes we'd point you to, ordered by best value and easiest to find.

items.name: Khao soi & nam ngiao at a local shop
items.blurb: Northern Thai staples you'll find all over Pai and Mae Hong Son. One bowl is filling and cheap — the best-value lunch for anyone on a tight budget.

items.name: Mae Hong Son morning market (kad chao)
items.blurb: Shan (Tai Yai) food for a few dozen baht — fermented soybean snacks, clear-broth rice noodles, Shan sweets. Graze your way through in the morning and fill up for under a hundred.

items.name: Pai Walking Street (dinner)
items.blurb: Street food runs the whole length of the street, savoury and sweet at easy-going prices. A dinner you can graze through without sitting down at a pricey restaurant.

items.name: Khao ram fuen / khanom jeen nam ngiao
items.blurb: Local Shan–Yunnanese dishes you can track down in Mae Hong Son, boldly flavoured in the local style and easy on the wallet.

items.name: Mantou & Yunnanese pork leg at Ban Rak Thai
items.blurb: If you head up to Ban Rak Thai, try the fried mantou buns with Yunnanese braised pork leg — a shareable plate that's good value and a flavour that's hard to find elsewhere.

items.name: Hill-grown coffee at a small Pai cafe
items.blurb: Pai is wall-to-wall cafes. If you want to chill without overspending, skip the famous view cafes with high prices and pick a small shop in town where hill-grown coffee runs from a few dozen to a hundred-odd baht.

items.name: Roti & roadside sweets
items.blurb: Cheap sweets you can find both on the Pai Walking Street and in Mae Hong Son town — a late-night fill-up for just a few baht.

items.name: Noodles at the Ban Ja Bo viewpoint
items.blurb: If you stop at Ban Ja Bo, try the legs-dangling noodles on the cliff edge with sea-of-mountains views. The bowl isn't expensive but the setting stays with you. Long queues at peak times.

blocks.title: Tips for eating cheap
blocks.html: The morning market opens very early and the good stuff sells out fast — get there before 8am for the full spread and the freshest picks. As for the famous view cafes in Pai, prices are often several times higher than the shops in town. On a tight budget, take your view photos and then go sip coffee at a small shop instead.

blocks.text: 3 days, 2 nights focused on Pai (budget edition)

blocks.html: This plan suits anyone with about 3 days. Take the minivan from Chiang Mai, base yourself in Pai, rent a scooter and explore around town. Most of the sights are free or charge a small entry fee of a few dozen baht.

items.activity: Catch the Prempracha minivan from Arcade, Chiang Mai → Pai
items.note: About ฿150, roughly 3 hours. Lots of curves — keep motion-sickness tablets handy

items.activity: Check in to a hostel near the Walking Street, drop your bags, rent a scooter
items.note: Rental ฿100–150 a day — ask your accommodation to help and you'll get a better rate

items.activity: Eat khao soi at a local shop, then stroll around Pai town
items.note: Lunch around ฿50–60

items.activity: Ride to the Pai Historical Bridge + Wat Nam Hu
items.note: Free entry. Rice-field photo spots along the way

items.activity: Head up to Pai Canyon (Kong Lan) for sunset
items.note: Free entry. The ridge trails get slippery — wear shoes with grip

items.activity: Graze the Pai Walking Street for dinner
items.note: Eat as you walk — about ฿60–100 a meal

items.activity: Ride up to the Yun Lai viewpoint for the morning sea of mist
items.note: Entry a few dozen baht. Very cold at dawn — bring a warm layer

items.activity: Head back into town for breakfast at the market or a rice-and-curry shop
items.note: Breakfast around ฿40–60

items.activity: Visit Tham Lod cave at Ban Tham Lod
items.note: Hiring a guide + a bamboo raft is the main cost of the day — split it as a group and it's cheaper

items.activity: Stop at a waterfall or hot spring on the way back
items.note: Many spots are free or charge little. Soak your feet and ease the aches

items.activity: Hit a small cafe in town, sip some hill coffee and rest your legs
items.note: About ฿50–70

items.activity: Dinner on the Walking Street + roadside sweets
items.note: Budget around ฿80–120

items.activity: Up early, catch the corners of the Pai morning market, return the scooter
items.note: Top up the fuel to where it was when you picked it up, to avoid extra charges

items.activity: Breakfast near your accommodation, check out
items.note: Breakfast around ฿50

items.activity: Take the minivan Pai → Chiang Mai
items.note: About ฿150, arriving Chiang Mai in the afternoon. Book ahead in high season

blocks.text: Want to continue to Mae Hong Son town? Add this leg

blocks.html: If you've got more than 3 days, it's well worth taking the minivan on from Pai to Mae Hong Son town to take in Ban Rak Thai, Pang Ung, and the old town around Nong Jong Kham. The main extra costs are the minivan fare and another 1–2 nights of accommodation.

blocks.label: Extra day
blocks.title: Mae Hong Son – Ban Rak Thai – Pang Ung

items.activity: Minivan Pai → Mae Hong Son town
items.note: Few departures — check times in advance. About ฿150

items.activity: Check in to a guesthouse around Nong Jong Kham, eat a Shan lunch
items.note: Central location, easy to explore on foot

items.activity: Visit Wat Jong Kham & Wat Jong Klang by Nong Jong Kham lake
items.note: Free entry. Beautiful in the golden evening light

items.activity: Head up to Wat Phra That Doi Kong Mu for evening city views
items.note: Free entry. The whole town laid out below you

items.activity: Next morning, go to Ban Rak Thai + Pang Ung for the mist over the lake
items.note: Without your own car you'll need to rent a scooter or share a ride — it's a long way and a mountain climb

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Ban Rak Thai and Pang Ung are far from town and the climb is steep. If you're not used to riding a scooter on mountain roads, sharing a minivan or songthaew with fellow travellers may be safer and better value than forcing it yourself. Ask your accommodation about shared rides.

blocks.text: Tips to push the budget down even further

items: Travel as a pair and split the scooter — halve the rental and fuel right away
Pick a dorm bed over a private room — saves several hundred a night, and you'll meet fellow travellers
Eat at the morning market and rice-and-curry shops — skip the famous view cafes that charge a premium for the setting
Stick mainly to free sights — the Pai bridge, Wat Nam Hu, Pai Canyon, Wat Jong Kham, Wat Phra That Doi Kong Mu are all free
Avoid peak high season if you can be flexible — the height of the cool season pushes room prices up and fills fast. Early or late in the cool season is better value
Book minivan tickets ahead when it's busy — so you don't miss a departure and end up chartering an expensive car

faq.q: How much does budget travel in Mae Hong Son and Pai cost?
faq.a: A 3-day, 2-night trip focused on Pai — staying in hostels, eating at local shops, and taking the minivan — can land around 2,000–2,800 baht per person. Add 1–2 days continuing to Mae Hong Son town and that's another 1,000–1,500 baht. The main variables are whether you take a dorm bed and whether you can split the scooter.

faq.q: Can I travel Mae Hong Son and Pai without my own car?
faq.a: Easily. Take the Prempracha minivan from Arcade station in Chiang Mai to Pai for about 150 baht, roughly 3 hours. Once you reach Pai, rent a scooter for 100–150 baht a day to get around town. If you want to continue to Mae Hong Son town there are minivans for that too, but with few departures, so check the times in advance.

faq.q: How much is a scooter rental in Pai, and is it safe?
faq.a: Prices start around 100–150 baht a day, plus 50–80 baht a day for fuel. Photograph the bike's condition when you pick it up and confirm the fuel level matches. Always wear a helmet. The roads around Pai town are easy to ride, but the climb up to Ban Rak Thai and Pang Ung is very steep — if you're not used to mountain roads, share a ride instead.

faq.q: When's the best time to go for value without overpaying?
faq.a: The views are best in the cool season, November to January, but the peak gets crowded and accommodation prices rise and fill fast. If you want to save money and still get cool weather, try early or late in the cool season — room prices come down and it's easier to book.

faq.q: Pai or Mae Hong Son town — which is better for a tight budget?
faq.a: If you're short on time and focused on saving, basing yourself in Pai is better value: cheap hostels, walkable street food, and lots of free sights nearby. Mae Hong Son town makes sense if you have more than 3 days and want to take in Ban Rak Thai, Pang Ung, and the old town around Nong Jong Kham.
